teams.heading: Jake White's Fiji assistant hunt still open, no appointment announced
teams.body: Jake White's search for a South African assistant to complete his Fiji staff remains unresolved. Mid-October reporting said White was turning to a trusted Springbok ally, but no name has been confirmed and no appointment has been reported since. Until that happens, the coaching group is incomplete, with the November block against France, Ireland and Italy the next test for the new set-up.

teams.heading: Brian Moore says Henry Pollock's Premiership brawl may affect Borthwick's starting choices
teams.body: Brian Moore has warned that Henry Pollock's needling during Saturday's Leicester-Northampton scuffle could cost him in Steve Borthwick's selections. Pollock wound up Tigers pair Ollie Chessum and Freddie Steward, and Leicester went on to win 28-7, scoring four tries after the flashpoint. Writing in the Telegraph, Moore said the episode "may have repercussions when it comes to Steve Borthwick's starting choices for the final rounds of next month's Nations Championship."

lead.why: A England player's conduct in a club flashpoint now carries a direct selection question for Borthwick before the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Galthié replaces Brau-Boirie, Gazzotti and Hastoy with Depoortere, Jelonch and Le Brun
teams.body: Fabien Galthié has had to reshape his extended squad for the Nations Championship, with centre Fabien Brau-Boirie, No. 8 Marko Gazzotti and flyhalf Antoine Hastoy all sidelined after Top 14 injuries, the French federation announced on Monday. Nicolas Depoortere, Anthony Jelonch and the uncapped Louis Le Brun are called up in their place. France already lack Matthieu Jalibert, Thomas Ramos and Julien Marchand, and open against Fiji before facing the Springboks and Argentina.

lead.why: It is the France men's XV squad story, with the replacements confirmed, and the other candidates are a Wales-based player or lack a France angle.

teams.heading: Ireland winger Robert Baloucoune commits Ulster future to at least summer 2029
teams.body: Ulster have confirmed that Robert Baloucoune, James McNabney and Joe Hopes have all committed to the province until at least the summer of 2029, good news for Andy Farrell's squad planning. Baloucoune's form earned him an Ireland call-up in the Six Nations, and he scored three tries as Ireland secured the Triple Crown. The 29-year-old was also named BKT Rising Star player of the Championship. McNabney, 23, is a recent Nations Championship squad call-up who returned from an ACL injury that ruled him out of 2025/26.

lead.why: The highest-scoring NEW item about an Ireland men's XV player, and it is not already covered in the editions on this tab.

teams.heading: Quesada says 17 Italy players unavailable as captaincy call nears
teams.body: Gonzalo Quesada put Italy's absences at 17 players at his Nations Championship launch press conference, up from the 12 Reuters reported last week. The head coach called it a serious difficulty, given that several of those players are core members of the group. He said a captaincy decision will come next week, with Giacomo Nicotera and Niccolò Cannone both having captained before. Tommaso Allan is building back toward full training as the team prepares for South Africa, Argentina and Fiji.

lead.why: Quesada's launch-press-conference comments are the freshest men's XV news, with a new injury count of 17 and a captaincy decision due next week.

teams.heading: Townsend feels belief over All Blacks he never had as a player
teams.body: Gregor Townsend says the belief against New Zealand that eluded him as a player is now in his squad. Recalling heavy defeats to the All Blacks in his playing days, including 62-31 and 69-20, he said, "I feel it in the players." Scotland have never beaten New Zealand, who have won 31 of their meetings. As coach, Townsend has lost all three meetings, each in Edinburgh, by 25-17, 31-23 and 22-17.

lead.why: A new Townsend angle on the New Zealand match that Scotland fans will want to discuss, and it is not a rehash of the squad announcement already covered.

teams.heading: WRU in talks with Premiership and RFU over two Welsh clubs joining
teams.body: Welsh rugby's structure may be about to change again: WalesOnline understands the WRU is in negotiations with Premiership Rugby and the RFU over two Welsh clubs joining the Gallagher Prem. The move could come as early as next season, though the following campaign is considered more realistic. For the Ospreys and Scarlets, already fighting to survive a proposed cut from four regions to three, it could change everything. The WRU's statement still commits to four URC teams until the end of 2027/28.

lead.why: A new, men's-only story about Wales's professional structure that two outlets are running and that could reshape the Ospreys and Scarlets.

teams.heading: Thomas Gallo out at least six months; Rodrigo Martínez called up
teams.body: Argentina have lost prop Thomas Gallo for at least six months after he dislocated his left wrist in Lyon's 31-27 win at Bayonne and had surgery on Saturday. Dragons loosehead Rodrigo Martínez, who has four Test caps, has come into Felipe Contepomi's squad as cover. It is another blow for the Pumas, with Santiago Carreras, who has 70 Test caps, set to miss the rest of the season after a serious knee injury for Bath.

lead.why: It is a team-specific injury story carried by two outlets, and it gives the reader a named replacement, while the NEW search item has no usable detail.

teams.heading: Les Kiss recalls Kurtley Beale, 37, five years after last Test
teams.body: Les Kiss has reached for a 95-Test veteran, calling Kurtley Beale into the squad to replace Hunter Paisami, who is unavailable for personal reasons. It is Beale’s first Wallabies squad since 2024, when an Achilles injury ended his season, and his last Test came against Wales in Cardiff in 2021. “With Hunter’s unavailability we’re excited by what Kurtley can bring to the group,” Kiss said. Beale will primarily cover inside centre, and Kiss has also pointed to his form for the Western Force.

lead.why: Beale's recall is a new squad story about Australia's own players, and it has not appeared in any of the previous three editions.

teams.body: Japan Rugby has named a 35-player roster for the Nation Series, a wider group than any match-day squad and a sign of who the staff is keeping close. Coverage in today's press has not carried the individual names or the reasons behind the choices, so the detail will have to come from the announcement itself.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie's staff investigate the All Blacks' growing injury list
teams.body: Rennie says the backroom staff are looking into the growing injury list, and calf problems are the concern. Jordie Barrett's withdrawal from the second Bledisloe Cup Test and Samisoni Taukei'aho's absence both came from calf setbacks. "Not all were necessarily just dealt to us; we're just trying to work out why we had five or six calves," Rennie said, pointing to training loads while players were away from the group. He also rejected suggestions the hits on Savea and Proctor were dodgy.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item about the All Blacks' own men's XV, and it puts the coach on the record about the injury problem.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus names six uncapped players in 37-man Springbok squad
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has named six uncapped players in a 37-man Springbok squad for the Nations Championship, with Kolbe, Etzebeth, Esterhuizen, Pollard and Fourie all unavailable through injury. Stormers director of rugby John Dobson put it simply: "If you want to become a Springbok, come here." Markus Muller, the 19-year-old Stormers centre, could break Frans Steyn's record as the youngest Springbok of the professional era if he debuts. The Stormers supply 12 of the 37.

lead.why: It is the strongest NEW item, corroborated by two outlets, and it covers the Springbok squad selection that shapes the coming Tests.
